topic: Should I build a fast local code-search CLI in Rust?

recommendation.reason: Your must-have (fast regex over large repos with .gitignore) is already best-in-class solved by ripgrep, which publishes its engine as library crates. Depend on those crates instead of reimplementing regex from scratch, and add the fuzzy (nucleo-matcher) and structural (tree-sitter) layers on top to get your unified standalone CLI without maintaining a fork.
recommendation.reusableOption: ripgrep library crates: ignore (gitignore-aware walker, 164M downloads) and grep-searcher / grep-regex (the fast line-regex engine, 13.6M downloads).
recommendation.biggestUnknown: Whether you will accept depending on ripgrep crates as the regex+gitignore foundation. If you insist on zero ripgrep dependency and reimplement the engine, the must-have becomes a multi-year performance chase against ripgrep with little likelihood of matching it.

competitors.name: ripgrep
competitors.overview: The standard fast Rust regex search tool, recursive over directories, natively respecting .gitignore. The user already uses it. Its engine is also published as library crates (ignore, grep-searcher, grep-regex), letting a new CLI reuse the hard parts without forking.

notableDesigns.title: ignore crate
notableDesigns.detail: Standalone .gitignore/.ignore matcher (164M downloads) usable as a dependency, giving gitignore-aware walking for free.

notableDesigns.title: grep-searcher / grep-regex crates
notableDesigns.detail: The fast line-regex engine published as libraries (13.6M+ downloads), so a new CLI can embed ripgrep-class search without maintaining a fork.

reusableLessons: Depend on ignore + grep-searcher/grep-regex as the regex+gitignore foundation of your standalone CLI.
Do not reimplement the regex engine; competing with ripgrep tuning from scratch is the expensive, low-odds part of this idea.
competitors.summary: ripgrep already solves your must-have better than a from-scratch rebuild likely can, and it hands you its engine as crates, so the build question reduces to adding the missing fuzzy and structural layers on top.
competitors.coverageNote: Verified via GitHub repo + crates.io download counts. Anonymous GitHub API only.

competitors.name: ast-grep
competitors.overview: A Rust CLI for structural (AST) code search, lint, and rewrite using tree-sitter patterns across many languages. Parallel and fast. It is the closest existing solution to your structural nice-to-have.

comparison.candidate: Unverified; walks project files but gitignore fidelity not stated on primary page.
Native; tree-sitter AST patterns, structural search/replace.

notableDesigns.title: AST pattern syntax
notableDesigns.detail: Write code-like patterns to match structure, not text; useful model for your structural layer UX.

notableDesigns.title: Parallel Rust engine
notableDesigns.detail: Demonstrates that Rust + tree-sitter can scale structural search across thousands of files.

reusableLessons: Study ast-grep pattern syntax and rule design as the template for your structural mode.
If structural search alone were enough, ast-grep already ships it, so your unified-CLI value is the combination, not structural in isolation.
competitors.summary: ast-grep already delivers your structural nice-to-have natively in Rust, but it cannot do regex or fuzzy, so it justifies a unified CLI only if combining all three matters to you.
competitors.coverageNote: Capabilities verified from ast-grep.github.io primary page. Cross-platform binary distribution not explicitly stated there. Anonymous GitHub API only.

competitors.name: nucleo-matcher
competitors.overview: A high-performance Rust fuzzy matching library, faster than fzf/skim/fuzzy-matcher, used by the Helix editor. It is a library, not a CLI, so it would be embedded inside your tool.

comparison.candidate: Native; Smith-Waterman scoring, faster than fzf/skim.
Library only; needs a wrapper CLI.

notableDesigns.title: Smith-Waterman matcher
notableDesigns.detail: Finds optimal matches more faithfully than fzf/skim and handles Unicode graphemes better.

reusableLessons: Use nucleo-matcher as your fuzzy engine rather than writing a scorer from scratch.
Pair it with a file/path source (e.g. the ignore crate walker) to get fuzzy-over-files behavior.
competitors.summary: nucleo-matcher gives you production-grade fuzzy matching as a Rust dependency, removing the need to build a fuzzy scorer yourself.
competitors.coverageNote: Verified from the nucleo README on GitHub.

unknowns: Whether you will accept depending on ripgrep crates (ignore + grep-searcher) as the regex+gitignore foundation, or insist on zero ripgrep dependency and a from-scratch engine.
Cross-platform binary distribution for ast-grep was not explicitly confirmed on its primary page.
Whether the unified one-CLI experience is valuable enough to you to justify the glue work over using ripgrep + ast-grep + a fuzzy picker separately.
